How it started

Zach began karting in April 2025 at TeamSport Bournemouth. Within four months he held the Cadet lap record at the circuit & at South Coast Karting.

The season in short

2026 so far…

Zach's 2026 began in the IKR Winter Series at Clay Pigeon Raceway: four finals, two wins, and the championship. In May he won the Wessex Challenge at the Clay Pigeon Kart Club and, with it, the gold WC plate worn by the reigning champion.

The summer took him nationally, to the Super One and UK Kart Series meetings against the strongest Honda Cadet fields in the country: a podium in the Super One final and the fastest lap of the final at the UK Kart Series. Back in the IKR Main Series he won the final at every round, 3 from 3, extending his run of club and regional final wins to five.

Away from the Honda Cadet, he raced the national SRK Cadet rental championship across 5 circuits and finished vice champion, and won the N32 Cup Endurance and the N32 Cup at Daytona MK.

Pace

Quicker than the median driver at every meeting

0.7s

a lap quicker than the median driver, measured over full race distance. Across 34 races with lap-by-lap data, Zach's average lap beat the median driver's in 32, and over a 12-lap race that adds up to 8.8 seconds. His best laps tell the same story: 0.7s quicker than the median driver, and ahead of them in 43 of 45 sessions.

The median driver is calculated by taking the average pace of the racing cohort. Half the drivers are quicker and half are slower. Beating their lap time means beating the average driver he raced against.

39.431s

The fastest Honda Cadet lap at Clay Pigeon in club racing, set on 22 Aug 2026. His best possible lap on the timing sheets is 39.372s, so there is more to come. Zach is coming for it again.

Racecraft

In the 2025 indoor regional final Zach was in a position to fight for the win. At just 10 years old he made the mature call: take second, and not get dragged into a fight he didn't need to win, because it could have cost him his place in the national final. He protected it, and finished 11th in the national final in his first year of racing.

Against the best

Ahead of the median national driver in every dry session

Rental karting

SRK Cadet Vice Champion

On identical arrive-and-drive karts there's no engine or setup advantage to hide behind: you have to work with the kart you are given, and the result is down to the driver. Racing against fields of up to 26 at 5 circuits across the country, Zach finished vice champion, and set the fastest lap of the day twice. After leading the championship mid-season, he missed out on the title after dropping a round to compete at the UK Kart Series.

P2best finish1 podium, 4 top-five finishes.
4/21heats wonOn the heat podium in 13 of 21.

5/7A finals reachedThe top-ranked final at 5 of 7 rounds.
  • 0.57s a lap quicker than the median driver on average across 7 rounds, on identical karts, and ahead of them at 6 of 7.
  • Within 1% of the fastest lap at 6 of 7 rounds, and the fastest driver on the day at 2 rounds (South Coast and Buckmore).
  • Fastest in all three sectors in the Buckmore A Final, with the fastest lap of the race.
  • Metronomic when it matters: the most consistent driver in the Hereford B Final, laps 4.0× tighter than the field, and won it. The same shows in club racing: in 36 of 42 sessions he got closer to his best possible lap than the median driver, just 0.06s off it against 0.14s.
  • Learns fast: on his return to Castle Combe he cut the gap to the fastest lap from 3.3% to 0.7%.
  • Team leader: top scorer for The Kartel at every round he raced, with 57% of the team's points.
  • Steadiest scorer on the team: across the Cadet and adult Challenge series, no Kartel front-runner finished more consistently. His finishing position moved by only ±2.6 places from round to round, against ±3.3 to ±6.5 for the team's adult drivers, and even his weakest round earned two-thirds of the winner's points.
